summary: Metadata encoding change causes pinned-session fingerprint mismatch and intermittent canary fallbacks
description:
Issue summary:
A change in client metadata encoding resulted in divergent canonical fingerprints between edge-proxy and control-plane. The divergence caused existing pinned sessions for customer NarrativeAI to intermittently lose affinity during a regional canary, producing transparent fallbacks to the default variant and causing degraded outputs and cost spikes.

Impact:
- ~6% of NarrativeAI production requests in us-east experienced transparent fallback to the default model variant during the canary between 2025-11-05 08:30 and 2025-11-05 11:40 UTC.
- Affected sessions saw mixed outputs and token-inflation (up to 1.6x tokens) due to fallback to a larger default variant.

Environment:
- prod (us-east)
- Dedicated tenant: NarrativeAI
- Routed through edge-proxy pool v3.2.1

Timeline (summary):
- 2025-11-05 08:18 UTC: NarrativeAI reported anomalous mixed model outputs via #support channel.
- 2025-11-05 08:42 UTC: Support triaged and opened this ticket.
- 2025-11-05 09:10 UTC: SRE flagged header normalization errors in edge-proxy logs.
- 2025-11-05 10:05 UTC: Eng reproduced fingerprint mismatch locally and pushed a candidate edge patch.
- 2025-11-05 11:00 UTC: Patch rolled to 10% edge capacity; fallbacks reduced.
- 2025-11-05 11:35 UTC: Full rollout to affected pools completed.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Tenant sends requests with route metadata header 'X-Model-Meta' encoded as URL-safe Base64 with trailing padding removed.
2) Edge-proxy receives header and performs normalization (current code path strips characters > 0x7F and NULs).
3) Control-plane computes canonical fingerprint by JSON-canonicalizing the decoded metadata using strict UTF-8 normalization.
4) Compare fingerprints between edge and control-plane; with the client variant encoding the fingerprints diverge and the session pin lookup fails, causing fallback routing to the default variant.

Note: This is reproducible with a synthetic request that includes non-ASCII metadata keys or values (e.g., emoji in custom 'note' field) and URL-safe base64 encoding without '=' padding.
logs:
[edge-proxy][2025-11-05T08:38:42Z] WARN route-fingerprint=mismatch tenant=NarrativeAI request_id=req_9f1a4
  expected_fp=8b3c1e2a8d... controlplane_fp=8b3c1e2a8d... edge_fp=9c5f7a0b2c...
[control-plane][2025-11-05T08:38:42Z] INFO computed_fp=8b3c1e2a8d... source=canonicalizer v=2.0.1
[edge-proxy][2025-11-05T08:38:43Z] DEBUG raw_header="eyJub3RlIjoi8J+RiCJ9" decoded="{\"note\": \"â\"}" , normalized="{\"note\": \"?\"}"
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: noisy-edge or cache TTL.
- Reproduced mismatch with synthetic client that sends URL-safe base64 metadata without '=' padding and includes a non-ASCII character in a metadata value.
- Root cause: edge-proxy normalization pipeline was performing a lossy ASCII-only sanitization step (stripping bytes >= 0x80, NUL truncation) before fingerprinting. Control-plane applies strict UTF-8 normalization and JSON canonicalization, so fingerprints diverged when metadata contained non-ASCII content or when clients used padding-omitted base64.
- Secondary factor: some client SDKs switched to urlsafe base64 (no padding) in a minor release the week prior (tracked to NarrativeAI SDK v1.6.0), which changed header byte sequences.
- Repro across versions: confirmed only for requests that both a) include non-ASCII values and b) use urlsafe base64 without padding. ASCII-only metadata unaffected.
- Risk assessment: Medium-high for tenants that include free-text metadata in route headers (customer-provided custom fields). Low for most self-serve users who don't set metadata.
resolution_notes:
Fixes applied:
1) Edge-proxy patch (PR 2412) updated the header normalization to: preserve UTF-8, decode urlsafe base64 with optional '=' padding, and canonicalize JSON with the same algorithm used by the control-plane.
2) Control-plane fingerprinting made tolerant to equivalence classes (treats unpadded urlsafe base64 as equivalent after decode) to reduce future coupling issues.
3) Backfilled telemetry to find other tenants with urlsafe base64 metadata and notified affected teams.

Rollout and verification:
- 2025-11-05 10:05 UTC: candidate edge-proxy image deployed to staging and validated.
- 2025-11-05 11:00 UTC: progressive rollout to prod edge pools; monitored canary for 30 mins.
- Post-deploy metrics: fallbacks for NarrativeAI dropped from 6% to 0.5% within the first 20 minutes; token inflation stopped.

Follow-ups and actions:
- Engineering: add unit tests for header encoding permutations and non-ASCII metadata (ticket INT-50988 created).
- SDK/Docs: draft guidance for clients to prefer standard base64 or explicitly document urlsafe behavior. Outreach to NarrativeAI to recommend SDK pin or upgrade.
- Runbook update: add a diagnostic query to edge logs to show canonicalization diffs (confluence page updated).

Postmortem: brief postmortem created at https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/63520/2025-11-05+metadata-fingerprint-mismatch (linked in confluence).
